court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
facts_of_case: The parties got married in 2017. The respondent/wife alleged that the petitioner/husband never showed interest in consummating the marriage and on one occasion scolded her in filthy language and attempted to forcefully sexually abuse her, leading her to leave the matrimonial home. The petitioner/husband filed a counter alleging that the respondent/wife had postponed consummation by stating she didn't want to get pregnant. The trial court granted a decree of divorce to the respondent/wife.

legal_principles.principle: Unwillingness to consummate a marriage at the inception amounts to cruelty.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, such unwillingness to consummate the marriage at the very inception of the marriage amounts to cruelty to the wife.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party who makes allegations to prove them.
legal_principles.held: From the very fact that it was only the respondent/wife who took up the issue with her parents and then thereafter with the relatives of the appellant/husband, the Trial Court came to the conclusion that non-consummation was on account of the fact that the respondent/husband was not willing.

outcome.final_order: The final order was that the appeal was dismissed and the decree of divorce passed by the Family Court, Salem in F.C.O.P.No.480 of 2018 was confirmed.

keywords: Latin maxim: actio non favet invenire
